I guess i could have explained that more, the oxygen in the fermentor can produce off flavors in the beer. When i set up my brew equipment, i got a couple of the 7-gallon buckets for my primary fermentors, and 5-gallon carboys as secondary fermentors. The large primary provides plenty of space for the kraeusen to form, and primary fermentation offgasses enough CO2 to purge the oxygen before it affects the brew (producing something like 90% of the final alcohol content in the process). In secondary fermentation, the yeast are much less active and won't produce a kraeusen so lots of headspace is not necessary, but they are still contributing to the final flavor of the beer.

As long as you sterilized everything properly, nothing is ruined, but you may end up with strange flavors.
